t: None of the funds provided by this Act shall be available to promote the sale or export of tobacco or tobacco products, or to seek the reduction or removal by any foreign country of restrictions on the marketing of tobacco or tobacco products, except for restrictions which are not applied equally to all tobacco or tobacco products of the same type.

fable.w: This is an appropriations limitation barring the use of funds to promote tobacco exports or to seek removal of foreign marketing restrictions. The tempting reading is that seeking action from a 'foreign country' involves an outside party, but the provision restricts federal advocacy abroad rather than bringing any outside party into a federal decision. It contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
fable.s: None of the funds provided by this Act shall be available to promote the sale or export of tobacco or tobacco products

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the use of federal funds for specific promotional or diplomatic activities regarding tobacco. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, states, or foreign entities) in the decision-making process. It simply limits what the government can do with its money.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds provided by this Act shall be available to promote the sale or export of tobacco or tobacco products, or to seek the reduction or removal by any foreign country of restrictions on the marketing of tobacco or tobacco products, except for restrictions which are not applied equally to all tobacco or tobacco products of the same type.

opus.w: This is an appropriations limit that bars funds from being used to promote tobacco sales or exports, or to push foreign countries to relax tobacco restrictions. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue for any outside party. The mention of foreign countries refers to the government trying to influence other countries' policies, not to outsiders taking part in a federal decision, so it is not participation.
opus.s: None of the funds provided by this Act shall be available to promote the sale or export of tobacco or tobacco products
opus.b:
This is a "No."

1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The section mentions a foreign country and the federal government asking that country to reduce trade restrictions. That could look like the government interacting with an outside party. It fails the definition because the provision only limits how funds may be spent. It creates no process in which outsiders are consulted, comment, sit on a panel, or can sue before a federal decision. Any contact with a foreign country would be the government lobbying someone else, not someone else taking part in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a spending restriction that prohibits the use of federal funds for promoting tobacco sales or lobbying foreign governments to remove trade restrictions. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as foreign governments, the public, or experts) in the decision-making process. The text merely defines what the funds cannot be used for.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds provided by this Act shall be available to promote the sale or export of tobacco or tobacco products, or to seek the reduction or removal by any foreign country of restrictions on the marketing of tobacco or tobacco products, except for restrictions which are not applied equally to all tobacco or tobacco products of the same type.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the restriction on funds implies a process where foreign countries or other entities could participate in deciding whether restrictions are applied equally, but the text itself is purely a prohibition on the use of federal funds for specific lobbying or promotional activities. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties.
